The Theme

What Prerna Means

Prerna is the Sanskrit-rooted word for inspiration — and it was chosen deliberately over words like "tribute" or "remembrance." A tribute looks backward. Prerna looks forward: it treats Gandhiji's life not as history to be observed once a year, but as a living source of ideas that still has something to say to a stadium full of people in 2026.

गांधी जयंती The two Hindi words for "Gandhi Jayanti" are literally reshaped into the two round lenses of his glasses — the seed the entire identity grew from.

The starting image is deliberately intimate rather than monumental: not a statue, not a portrait, but Gandhiji's glasses — the object through which he saw everything, and the single most recognisable silhouette of the man after the charkha itself. Turning the two Hindi words of "Gandhi Jayanti" into the two lenses is the founding move of the whole identity: it says, quite literally, see the day through his eyes.

The charkha (spinning wheel) sits beside it for a reason that goes beyond iconography. It was Gandhiji's chosen symbol of self-reliance — small, humble, and entirely in the hands of the person using it. Paired with the glasses, the two objects together say what the whole evening is trying to say: clarity of vision, paired with the discipline to act on it.

That pairing is rendered as a single radiant sunburst — warm maroon deepening to gold, like a sun rising over Dandi's own coastline at dawn, the moment the Salt March reached the sea. It is a mark about beginnings, not endings.

1

Satya — Truth

Represented through a photography competition, asking entrants to find and frame truth in the world around them.

2

Ahinsa — Non-violence

Given to the youngest attendees through a children's painting competition, so the value is learned by making, not just hearing.

3

Prerna — Inspiration

The theme becomes the subject itself in a poetry competition — asking what inspiration means to this generation.

Visual Directions

Finding The Mark

Three directions were explored to give this meaning a visual form — each a different bet on how much heritage versus how much energy the identity should carry.

Direction 01

The Vintage Postcard

Sketched heritage & postmark nostalgia — leans fully into memory and archive.

Direction 02

The Commemorative Stamp

Festive and decorative, built for print — closer to a keepsake than a stage mark.

Selected

The Sunset Emblem

Bold and radiant enough to hold a stage, legible enough to hold a lapel pin.

Why It Works

How The Theme Elevates The Experience

A theme earns its place only if it changes how the evening actually feels. Here is what this one is doing for the visitor, not just for the logo.

1

One Language, Every Touchpoint

The same emblem, palette and motifs recur from the moment a visitor sees the entry gate to the moment they scroll past a social post the next morning — so the event feels designed, not assembled, and every photograph taken on-site instantly reads as "Prerna" even without a caption.

2

History Made Legible, Not Lectured

Instead of plaques and paragraphs, the Dandi hut sketch, the charkha, and Gandhiji's own silhouette do the storytelling visually — at a glance, in a selfie, on a flag — so the history lands with a stadium of people, not just the ones who stop to read.

3

Participation Over Observation

The identity isn't just decor — it's built into things visitors do: a selfie booth built around Gandhiji's own words, a photography contest that puts a camera in their hand, a quiz that turns his biography into a shared moment rather than a plaque nobody stops for.

4

Warmth Instead Of Solemnity

The sunset gradient was chosen over a somber, funerary palette on purpose — Gandhi Jayanti is a public holiday people look forward to, and the warmth of the mark invites a family evening out rather than a memorial service.

The Design Assets

The Theme, In The World

Every surface at the venue — stage to signage — and every post before it, built from the one selected emblem.
